summary: Health Check at a Glance is a web-based health monitoring and guidance platform designed to help astronauts independently track and manage their well-being during long-duration space missions when immediate support from Earth-based flight surgeons is unavailable. The application features an interactive full-body model with Train and Treat modes for targeted exercises and step-by-step self-care guides, a color-coded Monitor mode for tracking vital signs and radiation exposure, and a Habitat panel for monitoring spacecraft environmental conditions like \text{CO}_2, oxygen, and cabin pressure. When abnormal readings require expert judgment, the system automatically generates and sends a summary to medical professionals aboard the ISS for review and approval. Inspired by NASA’s Human Research Program, the prototype currently uses simulated data for demonstration purposes, with future plans to integrate real-time wearable sensors and onboard spacecraft systems to promote early action and crew safety.
details: Health Check at a Glance is a web-based health monitoring and guidance application designed to help astronauts check, understand, and manage their own health during long space missions. The project aims to support crew safety by giving astronauts an interactive, easy-to-use platform that gathers their health information in one place, especially when they are far from Earth and help from flight surgeons is not immediately available. The application features an interactive full-body model where astronauts can click any muscle or body region to view its condition. Its Train mode shows exercises that target the selected body part, while the Treat mode provides step-by-step self-care guides for common problems such as sprains, burns, and nosebleeds. The Monitor mode displays health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, hydration, sleep, mood, and radiation dose, all color coded green, amber, or red so astronauts can read their status at a glance. Health Check at a Glance also includes a Habitat panel that tracks the spacecraft environment, including CO2, oxygen, humidity, cabin temperature, pressure, and radiation levels. When a reading needs a professional’s judgment, the system creates a summary of the astronaut’s readings and sends it to the medical professionals aboard the ISS, who review, verify, and approve the needed action. Inspired by NASA’s Human Research Program and its five hazards of human spaceflight, the project aims to connect with real wearable sensors and onboard monitoring data in future developments. Although its health readings are currently simulated for demonstration purposes and are not medical diagnoses, Health Check at a Glance promotes self-awareness, early action, and safer decision-making in space. Through technology and accessible health information, Health Check at a Glance aims to help astronauts stay healthy, informed, and mission-ready.
